newsitem.title: UK: End-Nov oversupply dogs Brent value, Med sour firm.
newsitem.headline: End-Nov oversupply dogs Brent value, Med sour firm.

text.p: North Sea crude remained under pressure from an overhang of end-month loadings and a narrowing arbitrage window to the United States, traders said.
Mediterranean sours firmed on limited supply and improved refining margins, but traders saw no end in sight for North Sea's weakness.
December Brent stood 13 cents higher at $23.11 per barrel at 1830 GMT, and the Dec/Jan spread was steady over the day around +35 cents.
Dated Brent fell 13 cents against Friday to trade as low as December Brent -48 cents. "That shows the wet market is not out of the doldrums yet," a trader said.

Forties changed hands at a firmer Dated Brent +15 cents, six cents above Thursday's deal, but the seller said the cargo was at a premium because it was the last in the month and had the buyer's name on it.
Several North Sea cargoes loading in November remained to be sold, but many traders doubted if Statoil would send a Brent VLCC to the U.S. since this arbitrage narrowed further on Monday.
West African levels held steady after easing back late last week. With NNPC due to announce their Dec prices prices later this week, deal levels were expected to be kept P+C.
Forcados was valued around Dated Brent +55 cents following a deal last week at +52 cents.

"It just depends on who buys the next one. We should see some move in the next day or two but I expect price levels to be kept quiet until the NNPC prices come out. As far as I know they (NNPC) have not started discussing where next month's levels will be yet," one trader said.
Urals, currently the most profitable crude for Med refineries, looked set to make further gains.
